what_its_for: Diroximel fumarate is used to treat relapsing forms of multiple sclerosis (MS) in adults. This includes clinically isolated syndrome, relapsing-remitting MS, and active secondary progressive MS. It helps reduce the number of MS flare-ups (relapses) and may slow the buildup of disability.
how_to_take: Swallow the capsules whole. Do NOT crush, chew, or open the capsules. Take this medicine with food to help reduce stomach upset. Taking it with a meal that contains some fat (like a small snack or full meal) may also help reduce flushing (warmth, redness, or tingling in your skin). Try to take it at the same times each day to build a routine.
dosing: The usual starting dose is 231 mg (one capsule) twice a day for the first 7 days. After that, your doctor will increase your dose to 462 mg (two capsules) twice a day, which is the regular maintenance dose. Always follow your doctor's specific instructions — do not change your dose without talking to your doctor first.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember — but only if it is still the same day. If it is already the next day, skip the missed dose and take your next regular dose at the usual time. Never take two doses at the same time or double up to make up for a missed dose.
storage: Store at room temperature between 59°F and 86°F (15°C to 30°C). Keep the capsules in the original container with the lid tightly closed. Protect from moisture and heat. Keep this medicine out of the reach of children and pets. Do not use it after the expiration date printed on the package.
what_to_avoid: Avoid taking this medicine on an empty stomach, as this can increase the chance of stomach upset and flushing. Avoid drinking alcohol while taking this medication, as it may worsen side effects. Do not take aspirin or other NSAIDs (like ibuprofen or naproxen) right before your dose thinking it will prevent flushing — talk to your doctor first. Avoid anyone who is sick with an infection, as this medicine can lower your ability to fight infections.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away if you experience: serious allergic reactions (swelling of the face, lips, tongue, or throat; difficulty breathing; severe rash or hives); severe flushing or itching that does not go away; signs of a serious brain infection called PML (progressive multifocal leukoencephalopathy) — such as sudden weakness on one side of your body, trouble thinking or walking, vision changes, or personality changes; signs of low white blood cell count (repeated infections, fever, chills); severe stomach pain, nausea, or vomiting; yellowing of the skin or eyes (signs of liver problems); or any new or worsening symptoms of MS.
when_it_works: This medicine starts working in your body right away, but you may not notice changes in your MS symptoms for several weeks or months. It works over time to help reduce the frequency of relapses and slow disease progression. Keep taking it even if you feel well — stopping it suddenly can make your MS worse. Your doctor will monitor your response with regular blood tests and check-ups.
special_populations: Pregnancy and breastfeeding: Tell your doctor if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding. The effects of this medicine on unborn babies or nursing infants are not fully known. Use effective birth control while taking this medicine and discuss your options with your doctor. Kidney or liver disease: Tell your doctor if you have kidney or liver problems, as your dosing or monitoring may need to be adjusted. Elderly patients: Older adults may be more sensitive to side effects — your doctor will monitor you carefully. Children: This medicine is not approved for use in children under 18 years of age.
